You are redesigning the PUBLIC-FACING pages of Nxeon, a premium cloud VPS hosting platform (Next.js 15 App Router + Tailwind v4) at /opt/nxeon. Read /opt/nxeon/CLAUDE.md first. The authenticated portals are already redesigned in a premium dark style (glassmorphism, deep navy #060a14, blue→purple gradients #3b82f6→#8a70fb, glow) using the design system in app/globals.css + components/ui/. Your job: make the public marketing site and legal pages match that premium quality and flow cohesively with the portals — think Vercel/Stripe/Railway/DigitalOcean marketing sites.

STRICT SCOPE — you may ONLY create/modify:
- /opt/nxeon/app/page.tsx (landing — rebuild premium)
- /opt/nxeon/app/(marketing)/** (new route group for features, pricing, about, contact)
- /opt/nxeon/app/legal/** (new: terms, privacy, aup, sla)
- /opt/nxeon/app/login/page.tsx and /opt/nxeon/app/register/page.tsx (polish to match; keep the existing <LoginForm/> and <RegisterForm/> from components/AuthForms.tsx — only restyle the surrounding page/shell)
- /opt/nxeon/components/marketing/** (new components)
Do NOT touch: app/dashboard, app/admin, app/api, lib/, worker/, prisma/, components/ui/, components/portal/, components/AuthForms.tsx, app/globals.css (use its classes, don't edit), any config. Do NOT run build/git/systemctl. You MAY run `npx tsc --noEmit` to self-check.

DESIGN SYSTEM (use, don't reinvent): classes in app/globals.css — .card, .glass, .btn-primary/.btn-secondary/.btn-ghost, .grad-text, .page-title, .section-label, colors navy-950/900/850/800/700, brand-300..600, accent-blue/accent-cyan; animations animate-fade-up. Primitives in components/ui/primitives.tsx (Badge, etc.) and charts in components/ui/charts.tsx if useful for a dashboard-preview mock. The NX logo is an inline SVG (see components/portal/Shell.tsx Logo — two gradient strokes forming N and X; reuse that markup). Font is the default; keep clean typography, generous spacing, rounded-2xl, subtle borders border-white/[0.06], glow shadows.

DATA: Pull live plans for pricing from Prisma — `import { db } from "@/lib/db"` then `db.plan.findMany({ where: { active: true }, orderBy: { sortOrder: "asc" } })` (read-only; this is allowed even though lib/ is off-limits to EDIT — importing is fine). Also `db.osTemplate.findMany` to show OS/panel/app logos count ("Deploy Ubuntu, Debian, AlmaLinux, Rocky, cPanel, Docker + more"). Use `export const dynamic = "force-dynamic"`. Money: cents/100.

BUILD:
1. **Landing (app/page.tsx)** — premium single page inspired by the screenshots the user shared (a "Blazing Fast Cloud, Built for Scale" style hero): top nav (NX logo, links to Features/Pricing/Docs placeholder/Company, Login + Get Started buttons), hero with big gradient headline + subcopy + dual CTA + trust badges (No credit card required / Instant deployment / 99.9% uptime) and a floating glassy "server status" card or dashboard-preview mock on the right, a feature grid (Blazing NVMe performance, Global-ready, Enterprise security/DDoS, Developer-friendly API/CLI, Automatic backups, One-click apps), a live pricing section (map real plans into cards, middle = "Most popular"), a "Deploy anything" section showcasing the OS/panel/app catalog (Ubuntu/Debian/AlmaLinux/Rocky + cPanel/Plesk/CyberPanel/Docker/WordPress with a tabbed or logo-cloud treatment), a "Everything in one beautiful dashboard" section, a final CTA band, and a rich footer (product/company/legal/social columns linking to your new pages). Smooth, responsive, animated on scroll-in (use animate-fade-up / CSS only — you can add a small "use client" IntersectionObserver component in components/marketing if you want reveal-on-scroll, but keep it lightweight and optional).
2. **/features, /pricing, /about, /contact** under app/(marketing)/ — each a polished page reusing a shared MarketingHeader + MarketingFooter component (components/marketing/). Pricing pulls real plans + a comparison table + FAQ. Features expands the grid with detail. About = company story/mission placeholder copy (mark clearly as placeholder). Contact = a simple styled form that posts to a mailto: or shows support email (no backend — note it).
3. **/legal/terms, /legal/privacy, /legal/aup (acceptable use), /legal/sla** — professionally-written, genuinely useful baseline legal copy for a VPS hosting company (clear headings, last-updated date, readable prose in .prose-like styling with max-width). These are REAL starting templates a host needs (prohibited uses, abuse, liability, data, uptime SLA credits). Add a clear top banner note on each: "Template — review with legal counsel before production." Link them from the footer.
4. **login/register pages** — restyle the shell around the existing forms to match (glass card, NX logo, subtle gradient background, a left-side value-prop panel on wide screens). Keep <LoginForm/> / <RegisterForm/> imports intact.

Every public page must share consistent MarketingHeader (with working nav to your pages, Login/Get Started) and MarketingFooter. No dead links — only link to pages you create + /login + /register. Make it genuinely beautiful and cohesive with the dark premium portal aesthetic. Mobile-responsive (hamburger nav ok). tsc clean.

Report: files created, and confirm tsc --noEmit passes.

1	# Nxeon — VPS hosting platform
2	
3	Hostinger-style VPS hosting platform running on this Proxmox VE 9 dedicated server (OVH KS-GAME, i7-7700K, 64GB RAM, 2×450GB NVMe ZFS mirror + 4TB HDD backup pool).
4	
5	## Architecture
6	
7	- **Web panel**: Next.js 15 (App Router, server actions) + Tailwind v4, served by `nxeon-web.service` on port 3000, behind nginx on port 80. Public IP: 51.79.162.96.
8	- **Worker**: `worker/index.ts` run by `nxeon-worker.service` (as root — it manages iptables). Polls the `Job` table every 3s and executes provisioning/lifecycle jobs against the Proxmox API.
9	- **DB**: PostgreSQL 17, database `nxeon`, Prisma ORM ([prisma/schema.prisma](prisma/schema.prisma)). Use `npm run db:push` after schema changes.
10	- **Proxmox**: API token auth (`nxeon@pve!platform`, creds in `.env`). Templates: VMID 9000 (Ubuntu 24.04), 9001 (Debian 13), cloud-init based, cloned onto ZFS storage `vmdata`.
11	- **Networking**: VMs attach to NAT bridge `vmbr1` (10.20.0.0/24, gateway .1). IPs allocated from 10.20.0.100–250 ([lib/ipam.ts](lib/ipam.ts)). SSH exposed via DNAT port forwards 20000–29999 in iptables chain `NXEON_FWD`, rebuilt from DB by [worker/network.ts](worker/network.ts) — never edit that chain by hand.
12	- **Cloud-init**: vendor snippet at `/tank/backup/snippets/nxeon-vendor.yaml` (installs qemu-guest-agent, enables root password SSH).
13	
14	## Portals & design system
15	
16	- Customer portal (`app/dashboard/**`) and admin ops portal (`app/admin/**`) are separate sidebar apps sharing `components/portal/Shell.tsx` (sidebar, topbar, notifications bell, ⌘K command palette backed by `/api/search`).
17	- Design system lives in `app/globals.css` (glass cards, gradient buttons, navy palette) + `components/ui/primitives.tsx` + `components/ui/charts.tsx` (dependency-free SVG charts). Use these — do not add chart libraries.
18	- Admin impersonation: `impersonateUser()` sets a signed cookie; `currentUser()` returns the target, `realUser()` the actual admin; banner + exit handled in Shell. Admin pages call `realUser`/`requireAdmin` and refuse to render while impersonating.
19	- Metrics come from Proxmox RRD via `/api/metrics` (node for admins, per-server for owners).
20	
21	## Integrations (activate via /opt/nxeon/.env)
22	
23	- **Stripe**: `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` + `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` → wallet top-ups switch from demo gateway to Checkout (`/api/stripe/checkout`, webhook `/api/stripe/webhook`, event `checkout.session.completed`, idempotent by session id).
24	- **Namecheap** (`lib/namecheap.ts`): `NAMECHEAP_API_USER/KEY/USERNAME/CLIENT_IP` (+`NAMECHEAP_SANDBOX=1` for testing) → domain search/register/renew/DNS management. TLD retail prices in `TLD_PRICES`.
25	- **GitHub**: remote `origin` = `git@github.com:santino1233/nxeon.git` via deploy key `/root/.ssh/nxeon_deploy`. Every commit auto-pushes via `.git/hooks/post-commit`. `.env`/credentials are gitignored — never commit secrets.
26	
27	## Conventions
28	
29	- All state changes to VMs go through `Job` rows — the web app never calls Proxmox mutation endpoints directly (read-only status calls are OK).
30	- One in-flight job per server (enforced in `serverAction`).
31	- Admin-only actions live in [lib/actions.ts](lib/actions.ts) and must call `requireAdmin()`.
32	- Free VPSes: `Server.isFree = true`, no billing, `expiresAt = null`.
33	- Wallet amounts are integer cents.
34	
35	## Commands
36	
37	- Build: `npm run build` (must pass before restarting services)
38	- Deploy after changes: `npm run build && systemctl restart nxeon-web nxeon-worker`
39	- Worker logs: `journalctl -u nxeon-worker -f`
40	- E2E test: `npx tsx scripts/e2e-test.ts` (orders a real VM; delete it afterwards via a DELETE job)
41	- Admin credentials: `/root/nxeon-credentials.txt`
42	
43	## Domains & TLS
44	
45	- **Single source of truth**: `/etc/nxeon/domains.env` (BASE_DOMAIN, ADMIN_HOST, STAGING_HOST, CERTBOT_EMAIL). The domain is a placeholder (`revsports.ca`) until the real one is bought. **Never hardcode the domain anywhere in app code** — the app uses `APP_URL` / `NXEON_ADMIN_HOST` from `.env`, and nginx vhosts are generated.
46	- **To migrate to a new domain**: edit `/etc/nxeon/domains.env`, point DNS (A records for apex, www, admin host, staging host) at the server, then run `scripts/configure-domains.sh`. It regenerates nginx vhosts, obtains Let's Encrypt certs, updates APP_URL in both `.env`s, and restarts web. That's the whole migration.
47	- **Routing**: customer portal on `https://BASE_DOMAIN` (admin path returns 404 here — hidden); admin ops portal on `https://ADMIN_HOST` (secret subdomain, root 302→/admin); staging on `https://STAGING_HOST`. HTTP→HTTPS 301. Real LE cert (auto-renews via certbot timer); self-signed fallback for bare-IP.
48	- Secure cookies are on (`COOKIE_SECURE=1`) now that real HTTPS exists. Stripe webhook is live at `https://BASE_DOMAIN/api/stripe/webhook`.
49	
50	## Environments
51	
52	- **Production**: `/opt/nxeon`, DB `nxeon`, services `nxeon-web` (port 3000) + `nxeon-worker`, nginx port 80, VPS pools IP 10.20.0.100–250 / SSH ports 20000–29999, NAT chain `NXEON_FWD`. Public: http://51.79.162.96
53	- **Staging**: `/opt/nxeon-staging`, DB `nxeon_staging`, services `nxeon-staging-web` (port 3001) + `nxeon-staging-worker`, nginx port 8080, ISOLATED VPS pools IP 10.20.0.50–99 / SSH ports 30000–30999, NAT chain `NXEON_FWD_STG`, VM tag `nxeon-staging`. Public: http://51.79.162.96:8080. Admin creds: `/root/nxeon-staging-credentials.txt`.
54	- Instance differences are driven entirely by `.env` (NXEON_ENV, NXEON_COOKIE_NAME, NXEON_NAT_CHAIN, NXEON_TAG, NXEON_IP_START/END, NXEON_SSH_PORT_START/END, NXEON_CRED_FILE, PORT, APP_URL) — the code is identical.
55	- **Deploy flow**: push to GitHub → `scripts/deploy-staging.sh [ref]` builds+migrates+restarts staging → verify at :8080 → `scripts/promote-production.sh` rebuilds+restarts production. The improvement agent should test changes on staging before promoting.
56	
57	## Safety rules
58	
59	- NEVER touch VMIDs 9000–9999 (templates) except to add new templates.
60	- Staging and production share the Proxmox node but never overlap: staging only ever allocates IPs .50–.99 and ports 30000–30999. Never point staging pools at production ranges.
61	- Test risky/provisioning changes on staging (`scripts/deploy-staging.sh`) before promoting to production.
62	- Never `qm destroy` a VM that has a `Server` row — always go through a DELETE job.
63	- Do not commit `.env`. Do not print the Proxmox token into logs or docs.
64	- Always `git commit` working states; never leave the tree broken — services restart from this directory.

Now I'm mapping out the component structure for the marketing section—I'll need a header with navigation and branding, a footer with multiple columns, a scroll-reveal utility, and a reusable logo component.

For the routing, I'm thinking about using a route group at `app/(marketing)/` with a shared layout that wraps the header and footer around feature, pricing, about, and contact pages. The landing page and legal pages sit outside this group, so they'll import the header and footer components directly to maintain consistent styling across the entire site.

I'm creating a reusable Logo component that accepts an `id` prop to avoid gradient ID collisions when multiple instances appear on the same page — the header logo gets one ID, the footer gets another, and so on. Keeping the header static with just Log in and Get Started buttons avoids any data fetching complexity. For the nav links, I need to resolve the conflict between linking to Docs and avoiding dead links — I'll either skip Docs entirely or replace it with an About page to stay consistent with the constraint of only linking to pages I actually create.

For the footer, I'm planning columns for Product, Company, Legal, and social icons, but I need to be careful with social links since those could also become dead links if not properly configured.

I'll render the social icons as decorative spans without href attributes to avoid broken links, keeping them visually present but non-functional. Now I'm moving on to build a lightweight Reveal component using IntersectionObserver for scroll-triggered animations, then laying out the landing page sections starting with the header and hero with a badge and gradient headline.

I'm structuring the page with a two-column grid on larger screens, featuring a glassy server status card on the right, followed by logo cloud, feature grid, pricing, deploy section with OS catalog, dashboard preview, final CTA, and footer. I need to check the chart component signatures to use them correctly for the mock server status and dashboard preview sections.

## Done — public-facing Nxeon redesign complete

Rebuilt the entire marketing + legal surface in the premium dark portal aesthetic (glassmorphism, navy #060a14, blue→purple gradients, glow), reusing the existing `app/globals.css` classes and `components/ui/charts.tsx` — no design-system files were edited, and all off-limits directories (dashboard/admin/api/lib/worker/prisma/components/ui/portal, globals.css, AuthForms) were left untouched.

### Files created

**components/marketing/** (all new)
- `Logo.tsx` — reusable NX mark + wordmark (unique gradient ids per instance)
- `MarketingHeader.tsx` — sticky glass nav, scroll-aware, mobile hamburger; links Features/Pricing/About/Contact + Log in/Get Started
- `MarketingFooter.tsx` — Product/Company/Legal columns + status line (no dead links; social icons are decorative)
- `Reveal.tsx` — lightweight IntersectionObserver reveal-on-scroll wrapper
- `icons.tsx` — server-safe line-icon set
- `sections.tsx` — `SectionHeading`, `FeatureCard`, `TrustBadges`, `CtaBand`
- `PricingGrid.tsx` — maps live plans to cards, middle = "Most popular"
- `HeroVisual.tsx` — floating glassy server-status card (uses Sparkline)
- `DashboardPreview.tsx` — dashboard mock (AreaChart/Donut/MeterBar)
- `DeployCatalog.tsx` — tabbed OS / control-panel / app catalog
- `ContactForm.tsx` — styled mailto form (no backend, clearly noted)
- `LegalDoc.tsx` — legal doc renderer with side nav + template banner
- `AuthShell.tsx` — two-pane auth shell (value-prop panel + glass card)

**Pages**
- `app/page.tsx` — rebuilt premium landing: hero + trust badges + status card, 6-feature grid, live "deploy anything" catalog (pulls `db.osTemplate`, falls back to 5 OS / 7 panels / 6 apps), live pricing, dashboard section, CTA band, footer
- `app/(marketing)/layout.tsx` + `features/`, `pricing/`, `about/`, `contact/` pages (pricing pulls live plans + comparison table + FAQ; about marked placeholder; contact notes no backend)
- `app/legal/layout.tsx` + `terms/`, `privacy/`, `aup/`, `sla/` — full baseline legal copy, each with a "Template — review with counsel" banner and last-updated date
- `app/login/page.tsx` + `app/register/page.tsx` — restyled shells via `AuthShell`, keeping the existing `<LoginForm/>`/`<RegisterForm/>` imports intact

### Notes
- Live data: landing + pricing use `export const dynamic = "force-dynamic"` and read plans/templates read-only via `@/lib/db`.
- Every public page shares the same header/footer; all links point only to pages I created plus `/login` and `/register` — no dead links.
- Mobile-responsive throughout (hamburger nav, responsive grids, horizontally-scrolling comparison table).
- Placeholder domain used only for the support email (`support@nxeon.cloud`), flagged in-page; no real domain hardcoded.
